picks.rationale: I did not expect to put an unapproved drug at rank 1, but the tolerability data made the argument for me: RASolute 302 showed fewer grade >=3 AEs on daraxonrasib than on chemotherapy (61.8% vs 69.6%) and a fraction of the TRAE discontinuations (1.2% vs 11.2%), alongside OS of 13.2 vs 6.6 months (HR 0.40, P<0.001) in the RAS G12 population that covers G12R. The safety base behind that is 168 PDAC patients at <=300 mg with grade >=3 TRAEs in 30%, mostly rash and GI events with workable management. Access through the FDA-authorized EAP (NCT07573215) means free drug under a monitored protocol, a very different risk posture from off-label improvisation. Two gates first: restaging has to confirm metastatic disease, and someone has to draw baseline labs, because no organ-function numbers exist in this chart since the resection.
primary_concerns: No long-tail safety record: first-in-human dosing started in 2022, so follow-up beyond about three years does not exist and there is no post-marketing experience anywhere.
The per-term grade >=3 AE table lives in the NEJM full text; what is priced here is the 61.8% union rate from the abstract.
Both the EAP and RASolute 303 require confirmed metastatic disease, and 303 adds a 6-week consent clock from the metastatic diagnosis; a locally-recurrent read on restaging closes both doors.
Undocumented organ function could fail EAP entry labs before the tolerability argument ever gets tested.

picks.rationale: The one option here with a safety record measured in decades of routine use rather than data cuts, and the AGEO cohort prices this exact class switch honestly: ORR 17.5%, mOS 8.8 months, grade 3-4 toxicity in 40% with no toxic deaths. Every adverse event it causes has a management algorithm any oncology clinic already runs. What I will not wave through is the neuropathy: AGEO reported 12.5% grade 3-4 neurotoxicity, and stacking a taxane on ungraded residual oxaliplatin neuropathy after 10 FOLFIRINOX cycles risks a permanent deficit, so a CTCAE grade goes in the chart before any first dose. It sits at rank 2 because the randomized comparison says daraxonrasib beats it on efficacy and on discontinuations at once.
primary_concerns: Nab-paclitaxel on top of ungraded oxaliplatin neuropathy; at documented grade >=2 I would drop the taxane or the regimen.
Starting chemotherapy can silently close first-line-style trial windows; RASolute 303 counts any new systemic line, so the screening calls come first.
An 8.8-month median OS floor is a thin offer for an ECOG 0 patient with a randomized alternative on the table.

picks.rationale: Of the CLDN18.2 routes, this is the one whose toxicity I can actually manage on paper: mostly hematologic (grade >=3 TRAEs 52.6% in the gastric phase 1, led by neutropenia at 28.4%), TRAE discontinuation 0.9%, no ILD, and no grade >=3 nausea or vomiting. The PDAC expansion, 44 patients at 6 mg/kg with CLDN18.2 >=60%, read out ORR 22.7% and mOS 9.1 months, which clears the AGEO benchmark without touching the neuropathy problem, and the phase 1 (NCT05458219) is recruiting at US sites. Compare satri-cel: 99% grade >=3 TEAEs, near-universal CRS, a gastric mucosal injury the mouse work never predicted, and no reachable access route anyway. Rank 3 rather than higher because the PDAC data are a conference abstract with no per-term grade >=3 table, and 60% sits exactly on the eligibility boundary under a different scoring convention than the resection report used.
primary_concerns: Per-term grade >=3 rates for the PDAC cohort are unpublished; the safety picture borrows from the gastric cohort.
Expression needs a fresh read on recurrent tissue: the trial tiers 1+/2+/3+ at >=60% while the resection was called 2+/3+ in 60%, and the recurrence has never been stained.
An exatecan payload lands after 10 cycles of irinotecan-containing FOLFIRINOX; topoisomerase-1 cross-resistance in that sequence is an open question with no published answer.

picks.intervention_label: olaparib maintenance, germline BRCA-mutated mPDAC (gated on pending germline panel)
picks.rationale: This pick exists mostly to keep the germline panel from slipping: guidelines call for dedicated germline testing in every PDAC patient, and the incidental tumor-NGS reporting here does not rule out BRCA1/2 or PALB2. If the panel returns positive and a platinum-containing regimen then holds the disease for >=16 weeks, POLO's maintenance route opens, and it is the best-characterized targeted option in this file: FDA-approved since 2019, grade >=3 AEs 40% vs 23% on placebo, 5% discontinuation, no new signals at the final analysis. The honest framing is chemotherapy-free time rather than survival; final OS was 19.0 vs 19.2 months. Low probability, deep familiarity.
primary_concerns: Inert until a germline panel is drawn; that blood draw should happen this week regardless of what the board picks.
Recurrence 4 months after oxaliplatin-containing adjuvant therapy argues against platinum sensitivity, which also lowers the prior on an unexpected gBRCA hit.
The maintenance route presumes a platinum re-challenge the rest of this dossier argues against.

notes: Two omissions were deliberate. Satri-cel holds the closest expression-matched efficacy signal in the file (two patients, one at 3+ in 60%), but 99% of treated patients in the randomized gastric trial had grade >=3 TEAEs, the preclinical package missed the gastric mucosal injury patients later showed, and no reachable access route exists; a two-patient letter does not buy that risk down. Zolbetuximab fails twice, on the 60% vs >=75% cutoff and on GLEAM's null OS (13.7 vs 13.6 months), so off-label use would be improvisation against negative evidence. Rezatapopt's registrational monotherapy cohort excludes KRAS-mutant tumors and every phase 1 responder was KRAS wild-type, so the Y220C route waits on the JAB-30355 class maturing. On weighting: the 0.7 efficacy/toxicity number is an assumed default the preferences file itself flags for revisiting, and ECOG 0 plus zero stated vetoes argues for active treatment, so I ranked for sequencing and gating rather than abstention. The gating workup (CTCAE neuropathy grade, CBC/CMP/bilirubin/CrCl, biopsy of the recurrence with CLDN18.2 re-stain and re-sequencing, germline panel) is cheap, fast, and opens or closes nearly every door above.

picks.rationale: HR 0.40 for OS, 13.2 versus 6.6 months, in a randomized phase 3 whose RAS G12 estimand contains G12R, and the drug is free right now under an FDA-authorized expanded-access protocol. Upside case: roughly a doubling of expected survival against an 8.8-month gem/nab-paclitaxel floor, without burning a trial slot. The weakness I will not paper over is that G12R was never analyzed on its own, and the matched GEMM work has G12R initiating tumors in about 10% of mice against rapid multifocal disease for G12D, so the allele-level effect could land well below the pooled HR. Staging decides access: the EAP and RASolute 303 both gate on confirmed metastatic disease, and 303 shuts its window 6 weeks after that diagnosis, so the site call has to be teed up before the biopsy reads out.
primary_concerns: G12R sits inside a pooled G12 estimand rather than a prespecified subgroup, and the 2L ORR of 35% rests on n=26 with a 95% CI of 17-56.
If the biopsy and restaging read locally recurrent rather than metastatic, both the EAP and RASolute 303 close on the same day.
The 6-week consent clock on RASolute 303 starts at metastatic diagnosis, which means outreach has to precede the pathology result.
Grade >=3 AEs were 61.8% (rash and GI dominate), and absorption of a once-daily oral after pancreatic resection has not been checked in this patient.
Going first with daraxonrasib closes KST-6051 and the other pan-KRAS phase 1s that require RAS-inhibitor-naive status.

picks.rationale: 22.7% confirmed ORR at 6 mg/kg in previously treated PDAC selected at CLDN18.2 >=60%, which is the largest prospective dataset any CLDN18.2 agent has in this disease. The scoring rule matters here: IBI343 counts 1+ and above, so a tumor with 2+/3+ in 60% of cells almost certainly scores above 60% on their scale rather than balancing on the cutoff. An exatecan payload kills without needing T cells, which is the argument for it in an MSS, TMB 0.83 tumor where every immune approach starts uphill. Against that: the number is a conference abstract with no per-term grade >=3 table, the registrational phase 3 is mainland China only, and the US door is a phase 1 whose live cohorts skew first-line.
primary_concerns: The 22.7% figure has no peer review and no toxicity breakdown; TEAEs ran 98.8%, led by anemia and neutrophil decreases.
Marrow reserve after 10 cycles of FOLFIRINOX is undocumented and this is a myelosuppressive payload.
CLDN18.2 on the recurrence is unmeasured, and concordance losses cluster in local recurrence; with biopsy sensitivity at 54.6% a negative stain would not settle it either.
US phase 1 slots may not exist for a previously treated PDAC patient even if the biology fits.

picks.intervention_label: ASP2138 (CLDN18.2 x CD3 2+1 bispecific T-cell engager)
picks.rationale: The >=1+ central IHC gate is the easiest CLDN18.2 door in this dossier for a 2+/3+ 60% tumor, there is a dedicated metastatic PDAC cohort across 46 sites, and archival tissue may start the screen while the biopsy is still being scheduled. Engagers can produce deep responses when they connect, and that ceiling is the reason to take a phase 1 that has published no PDAC efficacy at all. What exists is a 41.7% 12-week unconfirmed DCR in gastric, with CRS at 23.4% in the PDAC cohort and no grade >=3 gastritis on monotherapy. My real worry is mechanistic rather than regulatory: across syngeneic models, pretreatment intratumoral T-cell density drove BiTE response, and PDAC is exactly where that density bottoms out.
primary_concerns: No PDAC efficacy readout has been shown; the 41.7% DCR is gastric and unconfirmed.
Monotherapy arms exclude locally advanced unresectable disease, so a non-metastatic staging call closes this too.
On-target gastric mucosal injury and CRS in a patient whose upper GI anatomy is already surgically altered.
Source is a congress abstract whose identifiers could not be verified against Crossref.

picks.rationale: With PYNNACLE's registrational monotherapy cohort excluding known KRAS SNVs, this is the Y220C door that stays open, US sites recruiting and no KRAS exclusion posted. I am ranking an eligibility fact, not an effect size. The public record is one sponsor sentence about a positive efficacy signal at high dose, and nothing has been published since. Mechanistically I expect less than the target promises, since restoring p53 in KRAS-driven tumors with low mitochondrial priming produces cell-cycle arrest rather than apoptosis, and every rezatapopt phase 1 responder was KRAS wild-type. Still worth the screening call, because ECOG 0 travels well in dose escalation and the variant is the one this chemistry was built around.
primary_concerns: Zero published effect size: no paper, no abstract, no posted results, so there is no toxicity profile to weigh either.
The KRAS co-mutation that keeps rezatapopt's responders wild-type is the same one this patient carries.
Needs confirmation that Y220C persists in the recurrence; ctDNA would answer that without a needle.
Dose escalation can assign a subtherapeutic dose, and this class already showed secondary TP53 alterations in cis with Y220C at progression.

picks.intervention_label: mKRASvax + balstilimab + botensilimab (mutant-KRAS peptide vaccine with dual checkpoint blockade)
picks.rationale: G12R is in the peptide pool, the mandatory ECOG 0 is a criterion this patient actually holds, and the Fc-enhanced CTLA-4 partner has produced responses in MSS disease where single-agent PD-1 blockade does nothing. AMPLIFY-201 proved G12R-specific CD4 and CD8 immunity can be raised in PDAC patients, though its HR 0.12 for RFS is a T-cell-threshold split inside a single-arm MRD trial, not a treatment effect. That MRD framing is the catch: a radiographic pancreatic mass is not minimal residual disease, and vaccines rarely shrink bulk pancreatic tumors. I would keep the Hopkins coordinator conversation warm as a post-cytoreduction move rather than pretend it competes with daraxonrasib now.
primary_concerns: Single US site in Baltimore, and the posted prior-therapy clause wants 4 to 6 months of first-line therapy for metastatic disease, which perioperative FOLFIRINOX may not satisfy.
On-treatment biopsy requirement runs into the vascular invasion around the recurrent mass.
No efficacy data for this construct in PDAC; the supporting HR comes from a different vaccine in a different disease state.
Dual checkpoint blockade brings immune-related toxicity in a patient whose organ function is entirely undocumented.

notes: Two things I left off the ranking on purpose. Satri-cel has the highest ceiling in the CLDN18.2 file (ORR 38.8% across GI cancers, and the published PDAC case with 3+ in 60% of cells had lung target lesions clear), but there is no door: the North American trial is closed, the NMPA approval is a gastric label dispensed only in China, and CARsgen has published no named-patient route. Someone should still email PR@carsgen.com, because the expression match is uncanny. Zolbetuximab is finished here on both counts, 60% against a 75% CDx cutoff and a GLEAM readout of 13.7 versus 13.6 months. Everything above is contingent on the EUS biopsy with core passes for NGS plus CLDN18.2 IHC, and on how restaging classifies the recurrence, since metastatic versus locally recurrent flips access for daraxonrasib and ASP2138 in the same stroke.

picks.intervention_label: daraxonrasib (RMC-6236, pan-RAS(ON) inhibitor) via RASolute 303, the phase 1/2, or the FDA-authorized expanded-access programme
picks.rationale: The only option in this dossier with a randomized survival win in exactly this population: OS 13.2 vs 6.7 months (HR 0.40) in previously treated RAS G12 PDAC, and the mechanism covers G12R where every allele-selective program does not. It also clears every stated preference at once: the patient wants trials and will travel, RASolute 303 is recruiting, the phase 1/2 stays open, and the FDA-authorized EAP supplies drug free of charge if no slot materializes. Oral dosing with rash and GI events as the main grade >=3 toxicities steers around the one toxicity this patient most likely already carries, the ungraded oxaliplatin neuropathy. Nothing else here comes close on evidence, and nothing in the preference file argues against it.
primary_concerns: Every fast route is gated on confirmed metastatic disease: the EAP and RASolute 303 both require it, so a local-only read on restaging closes both and leaves the phase 1/2 as the door.

RASolute 303 requires consent within 6 weeks of the metastatic diagnosis. The site call has to be teed up before the biopsy result lands; running the workup first and the outreach second could close this door by scheduling alone.
A G12R-specific resistance path (EGFR/RAS-WT rebound) is already described (pmid:42465401, preprint), so the post-progression plan should be drafted at the start, not at progression.

Preference fit: trials-first and travel fully satisfied; no toxicity veto in play. The 0.7 efficacy weight is an assumed default rather than the patient's number, but this pick wins under any plausible weighting.

picks.intervention_label: IBI343 (CLDN18.2 ADC, exatecan payload), phase 1 NCT05458219 with US sites
picks.rationale: The best-evidenced CLDN18.2 route this patient can actually reach: ORR 22.7% in previously treated PDAC (n=83), the largest prospective dataset for this target in this disease, with the phase 1 recruiting at US and Australia sites. CLDN18.2 at 2+/3+ in 60% of cells is the strongest handle the user asked us to work, and a topoisomerase-payload ADC does not lean on the checkpoint biology this MSS, TMB-low tumor lacks. The honest caveats: the registrational phase 3 is mainland-China only, so US access rides on phase 1/2 cohorts, and whether a 60% archival result clears the cohort's expression tier needs sponsor confirmation before anyone books travel.
primary_concerns: Cohort expression thresholds are sponsor-defined and the dose-optimization cohorts prefer moderate-to-high expressers; where 60% 2+/3+ lands is unconfirmed.

The stain is from the pre-adjuvant primary. Biopsy sensitivity for CLDN18.2 runs around 54.6% (pmid:40694660), so a negative stain on a small recurrence specimen should not be read as loss of the target.
GLEAM's negative zolbetuximab result in PDAC tempers the antibody class; the ADC mechanism differs, but expectations should carry that context.
Preference fit: trial route, US-reachable, no veto or modality conflict. Fully inside the stated preferences.

picks.rationale: The widest-open CLDN18.2 door: the PDAC monotherapy arm takes patients with no line limit, the >=1+ escalation cutoff sits far below this tumor's 60% at 2+/3+, and 46 sites across the US, Japan, Europe, and Asia suit a patient who said travel is fine. The efficacy shown so far is gastric and abstract-level (12-week DCR 41.7% at >=420 ug) with the PDAC readout still pending, so this is an access-and-fit pick rather than an evidence pick, and the patient deserves that distinction stated plainly.
primary_concerns: No PDAC efficacy data exist yet for this drug; ranking it above better-published options would be selling hope, which is why it sits third.
CD3-engager class toxicity (CRS) has no published PDAC-specific characterization here.
Monotherapy arms exclude locally advanced unresectable patients, so the staging read decides which arms are even open.
Preference fit: clean on every stated axis; the only friction is the ungraded neuropathy, which several protocols cap at grade 1 and which must be graded before screening anywhere.

picks.rationale: Insurance for the scenario where daraxonrasib's doors fail on staging: this phase 1 names G12R explicitly, writes down the exact line-counting rule this recurrence satisfies (adjuvant therapy with recurrence inside 6 months counts as the prior line), and takes locally advanced unresectable disease as well as metastatic. IV administration also sidesteps any post-Whipple oral-absorption question the undocumented organ function leaves open. It is dose escalation with zero published effect sizes; I am ranking eligibility fit and executability here, and saying so.
primary_concerns: Escalation slots and dose levels move week to week, and early cohorts carry sub-therapeutic-dose risk.

Sequencing trap: several pan-KRAS trials exclude prior RAS-inhibitor exposure, so this class of door mostly closes after daraxonrasib; AN9025's backfill cohorts (nct:NCT07252479) are the rare post-pan-RAS(ON) exception worth remembering.
Preference fit: trial-first and travel-tolerant, satisfied. No published toxicity profile yet to weigh against the assumed 0.7.

picks.intervention_label: JAB-30355 (oral p53 Y220C reactivator), phase 1/2 NCT06386146
picks.rationale: The user asked for every variant kept on the table, and this is what the TP53 Y220C axis actually offers: rezatapopt's registrational monotherapy cohort excludes any KRAS SNV, so G12R blocks the flagship, and JAB-30355 is the US-recruiting reactivator with no posted KRAS exclusion. Its entire efficacy record is one sponsor phrase, 'positive efficacy signal', with nothing published as of August 2026. I rank it because the preference file says trials first and this keeps a second biological axis live, not because anyone should expect a known effect size.
primary_concerns: Zero published effect sizes; even rezatapopt's phase 1 responders were exclusively KRAS wild-type, so reactivator benefit in a KRAS-co-mutated tumor is unproven at best.
The registry posts no KRAS exclusion but the full protocol might; confirm with the sponsor before any screening trip.
Needs Y220C persistence confirmed in the recurrence (ctDNA acceptable) plus a baseline echo, since LVEF <=50% excludes.
Preference fit: satisfies trials-first and the user's keep-every-variant instruction; NTS071 (nct:NCT07060989) gives this axis redundancy if this door narrows.

notes: Execution order matters more than the ranking here. Send the germline panel now: it is a blood draw NCCN recommends for every PDAC patient and it gates olaparib maintenance later. Pre-alert the nearest RASolute 303 site before the biopsy result returns, because the 6-week metastatic-diagnosis clock starts at staging, not at our convenience. The recurrence biopsy unlocks the CLDN18.2 re-stain, the re-sequencing, and most trial screens; grade the oxaliplatin neuropathy at the same visit since several protocols cap it at grade 1. Two accounting items so nothing the user asked for gets silently dropped: KMT2C S2816fs has no clinical route anywhere in this dossier (zero trials, preclinical hypotheses only), and ranking one would be false hope, so it stays named but unranked; the MSS/TMB-low negative is honored by routing immunotherapy interest through engager and vaccine mechanisms rather than checkpoint blockade, which the biomarker file forecloses. Satri-cel and the IBI343/FG-M108 phase 3s are China-only doors a US patient cannot realistically walk through, and any ranking that treats them as reachable is selling geography the access file contradicts. Last: the 0.7 efficacy/toxicity weight is an assumed default, not the patient's stated number. My ranking survives any reasonable weight, but the board should not cite 0.7 as if the user chose it, and equally should not use its assumed status to discount efficacy for an ECOG 0 patient who asked for trials.

picks.rationale: RASolute 302 is the only RCT-grade evidence in this dossier that is in PDAC and contains this allele: n=500, mOS 13.2 vs 6.6 months in the pre-specified RAS G12 population, HR 0.40, P<0.001. G12R sits inside that estimand but was never studied as a population, no allele-resolved efficacy has been published, neither RMC-7977 paper has a G12R arm (the KPC work is Kras G12D-driven), and the only G12R-specific daraxonrasib data is an un-peer-reviewed bioRxiv preprint. Two transfer problems that nobody has closed: eligibility required metastatic disease, which an unbiopsied pancreatic-body mass has not been shown to be, and the trial population had prior therapy for advanced disease where this patient's only exposure is perioperative. It still ranks first for me, because a doubled median OS on a pre-specified primary endpoint outranks everything else in this file even after both discounts.
primary_concerns: RoB 2, measurement of the outcome: RASolute 302 is open-label. OS survives that, but the PFS estimate (7.3 vs 3.5 months, HR 0.45) carries detection-bias risk and the abstract does not say the reads were blinded.

Calling it replicated overstates the case. RMC-6236-001 shares sponsor and senior authorship with the phase 3, so ORR 35% (95% CI 17-56) in 26 second-line RAS G12 patients is internal support rather than independent confirmation, and that CI is 39 points wide.

Disclosure: no CT.gov results posted at review, and I have only the abstract-level extraction of the NEJM paper. I have not read the full text, so I cannot honestly score the deviations-from-intended-intervention or missing-outcome-data domains.

On the allele, the correction runs both ways. PMID 41556816 and PMID 31649109 describe tumour initiation and p110alpha binding, not response to RAS(ON) inhibition, so that work does not license a downgrade of the expected effect any more than the trial licenses a G12R point estimate. What it licenses is a wider interval than the HR 0.40 implies.

picks.rationale: The 44-patient dose-expansion cohort is the largest prospective CLDN18.2 efficacy dataset in previously treated PDAC, and it is a single-arm phase 1 reported in an ASCO abstract with no CI on the 22.7% confirmed ORR and no per-term grade >=3 table. Its mOS of 9.1 months does not separate from the 8.8 months (95% CI 6.2-9.7) that a plain gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel class switch produced after FOLFIRINOX failure in the AGEO cohort (cross-study comparison, but somebody should say it before 22.7% gets called impressive). The mOS 12.1 in the 17 patients with one prior line is an unadjusted subgroup at n=17 and I would not plan around it. Second because the randomized trial that would settle this is actually running and the phase 1 has US sites open, not because the current number has persuaded me.
primary_concerns: Indirectness on the biomarker: the efficacy cohort was defined as CLDN18.2 1+/2+/3+ in >=60% of cells, pooled across intensities. This patient's report says 2+/3+ in 60% from a clone the report never names, so 'clears the cutoff' is an assumption rather than a match.

Archival tissue is doing the selecting. Recurrent lesions matched the primary in 83.3% of cases and the losses clustered in local recurrence and liver metastases (PMID 40694660), so roughly one in six risk of target loss is weighted against exactly this presentation.

GLEAM (n=393) missed OS at 13.7 vs 13.6 months in >=75% expressers and exists only as a topline release with nothing posted on CT.gov. It bears most directly on a naked antibody rather than on an exatecan payload, but it is the only randomized CLDN18.2 readout in PDAC and it cannot be audited by anyone outside the sponsor.

Kerper (PMID 42080920) found positivity less common in neoadjuvant-treated resections. Cross-sectional, so it cannot separate treatment-induced antigen loss from selection, and this tumour has since taken four more cycles.

picks.rationale: CT041-ST-01 is the only randomized win anywhere in the CLDN18.2 class: n=156, mPFS 3.25 vs 1.77 months, HR 0.37 (0.24-0.56), P<0.0001. It is gastric, open-label, PFS-primary, and the absolute gain is about six weeks against a physician's-choice arm, with grade >=3 TEAEs in 87 of 88 treated patients. The PDAC record is a two-patient research letter, one of whom stained 3+ in 60%, which is an expression match and not an effect estimate. Third on strength of design alone; the North American study is closed to enrolment, so this is a sponsor question rather than a plan.
primary_concerns: Open-label design with an active-comparator physician's-choice arm and PFS as the registrational endpoint is the combination most exposed to assessment bias under RoB 2. OS was not what the trial was built to prove.

Cross-tumor extrapolation carries the entire argument. PDAC is desmoplastic and T-cell poor, and the construct's preclinical package (PMID 30203099) is gastric xenograft work whose clean mouse safety did not predict the gastric mucosal injury patients later had.
Toxicity is not a footnote at 99% grade >=3 and CRS in 95%, on top of modelled on-target gastric injury (PMID 41176533), in a patient whose post-resection upper-GI anatomy is nowhere in the record.
The single-arm base (PMID 38830992, n=98) reports mOS 8.8 months across GI cancers, which is the same neighbourhood as a chemotherapy class switch.

picks.rationale: Y220C is a real variant with a real drug class, and this patient can reach neither of the things that have data behind them. The registrational rezatapopt monotherapy cohort excludes any known KRAS SNV, and in the published phase 1 (n=77) every responder was KRAS wild-type: ORR 30% in KRAS-WT at >=1150 mg against 20% overall. JAB-30355's whole efficacy record is one sponsor phrase about a signal at high dose, with nothing published and nothing posted, so ranking it says something about an open door and nothing about evidence. Fourth, and it does not move up until a number with an n attached exists.
primary_concerns: There is no published effect size for any Y220C reactivator in a KRAS-mutant tumour, in any indication. The phase 1 report as extracted does not give the KRAS-mutant denominator, so zero responders among them is weak evidence of no effect rather than proof of none, and I am reading the abstract, not the full paper.
Sponsor-only disclosure with no independent analysis and no registry results is the reporting-bias scenario in its purest form. NTS071 (NCT07060989) is thinner still, with no source of any kind.

Even granting target engagement, the Sanchez-Rivera work (PMID 34074758) argues a KRAS-driven, low-priming tumour may arrest rather than die when p53 function returns. Mouse lung and sarcoma lines, so I am not weighting it heavily, but it points the same way as the clinical responder pattern.
Resistance to this class is on-target and heterogeneous (PMID 41504628), so a second-generation reactivator likely inherits much of it.

notes: What I did not rank, and why. ELI-002: the HR 0.12 for RFS is a threshold split on immune response inside a single arm, which is a biomarker correlation and not a treatment-effect estimate, and AMPLIFY-7P screens out patients whose CT shows recurrence, which is what this patient has. Zolbetuximab: 60% is below the 75% CDx cutoff and GLEAM was flat, so both eligibility and effect fail. FG-M108: the phase 3 cutoff (>=40% at >=2+) is the one this tumour actually clears, but the trial is not yet recruiting at a single mainland-China site and the supporting 1b is a single-arm ORR of 32.4% (n=39) on a gem/nab-paclitaxel backbone, which cannot isolate the antibody's contribution. ASP2138: the reported gastric readout is a 12-week unconfirmed DCR of 41.7%, about the softest endpoint in this file, and the PDAC cohort has contributed safety only. AZD0901: the pancreatic expansion exists and its data do not, and the posted cohort requires >=6 months from adjuvant to progression against this patient's roughly 4. Eight interventions in the dossier (JAB-30355, NTS071, GenSci128, spevatamig, FG-M108, ASP2138, ASP5834, KST-6051) have no indexed preclinical publication at all. KMT2C is not a handle: the one credible paper is gastric, uses double Kmt2c/d knockout plus Pten deletion, and no agent selects on KMT2C status. Two comparator points the board should not repeat carelessly. The 20% one-year post-recurrence survival figure comes from a cohort that excluded neoadjuvant-treated patients and used gemcitabine-era adjuvant therapy, so quoting it at this patient is a population mismatch. And there is no randomized rechallenge-versus-switch trial in this window at all; Tiriac (PMID 29853643) argues on per-agent organoid signatures that FOLFIRINOX failure should not be assumed to predict gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel failure, which is a caution against confident sequencing language in either direction. Two open gates worth stating plainly: the germline panel has not been run, and POLO (PMID 31157963, PMID 35834777) is RoB 2 low with its pre-specified PFS primary met at HR 0.53 and a null final OS (19.0 vs 19.2 months, P=0.3487), so a positive gBRCA result would put genuinely high-quality randomized evidence on the table where none of my four picks has any. Everything above is scored on a specimen taken before four more cycles of chemotherapy, from a lesion that is not the one being treated.

picks.intervention_label: daraxonrasib (RMC-6236) via expanded access (NCT07573215) or RASolute 303 / phase 1-2 enrollment
picks.rationale: No guideline names daraxonrasib yet: NCCN Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma v2.2026 (April 22, 2026) went to press before the RASolute 302 publication (mOS 13.2 vs 6.6 months, HR 0.40, P<0.001 in the RAS G12 population) and the July 2026 NDA acceptance. What the guidelines do say for a recurrence inside 6 months of adjuvant completion is switch regimens, with trial enrollment preferred, and this pick is trial-or-EAP enrollment. The FDA-authorized expanded access protocol is listed as available and RASolute 303 counts an adjuvant-only history as first-line. I expect NCCN to add this within a cycle or two of FDA action; today it rides on the trial-preferred clause, not on a listed regimen.
primary_concerns: Both the EAP and RASolute 303 require confirmed metastatic disease, and NCCN wants suspected recurrence confirmed by imaging and/or biopsy anyway, so the unbiopsied radiographic mass keeps this patient outside every relevant population until the EUS biopsy and staging are done.
Whether adjuvant FOLFIRINOX with recurrence at 4 months satisfies the EAP's prior-line rule is a sponsor question; trial conventions mostly count it, but nothing in guideline text settles it.
As of August 2026 this sits in no NCCN, ESMO, or ASCO text, so no evidence category can honestly be assigned; the endorsement here is anticipatory.

picks.intervention_label: gemcitabine + nab-paclitaxel (guideline-endorsed class switch after FOLFIRINOX)
picks.rationale: The one regimen NCCN, ESMO, and ASCO all currently endorse for this sequence. ESMO's Express Update (ESMO Open, April 2025) grades gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel after FOLFIRINOX I, B for ECOG 0-2; ASCO's 2020 metastatic update reads the same for ECOG 0-1; and NCCN's recurrence pathway sends a recurrence inside 6 months of adjuvant completion to an alternative regimen, which after 10 FOLFIRINOX cycles means gemcitabine-based. The benchmark is modest (ORR 17.5%, mOS 8.8 months in the AGEO cohort), which is why the consensus documents treat it as the floor experimental options must beat. No validated ESMO-MCBS score exists for the second-line use, so I am not quoting one.
primary_concerns: Guideline text presumes confirmed recurrent or metastatic disease; this mass is radiographic-only, so biopsy confirmation comes first.
The residual oxaliplatin neuropathy is ungraded after 10 FOLFIRINOX cycles, and the AGEO cohort logged 12.5% grade 3-4 neurotoxicity on top of exactly that kind of baseline.
Starting chemotherapy quietly closes the first-line-defined trial windows (RASolute 303 among them), a sequencing cost no guideline page prices in.

picks.intervention_label: IBI343 (CLDN18.2 ADC) via phase 1 PDAC cohort (NCT05458219)
picks.rationale: CLDN18.2 in pancreatic cancer is guideline-silent territory, and I want that on the record: NCCN's CLDN18.2 text lives in Gastric Cancer v3.2026 at the 75% zolbetuximab cutoff, and the PDAC trial guidelines would have weighed (GLEAM) missed its OS endpoint. Where guidelines are silent their own default is a trial, and IBI343 carries the most prospective data in treated PDAC of any CLDN18.2 agent (confirmed ORR 22.7%, mOS 9.1 months at >=60% expression, the boundary this tumor sits on) plus a randomized phase 3 already enrolling. That phase 3 is China-only, so the realistic US door is the phase 1 PDAC cohort.
primary_concerns: The 60% 2+/3+ call is archival, from the December 2025 resection, on an unstated assay; the sponsor's central IHC on recurrence tissue could land either side of its cohort threshold.
The PDAC efficacy data are a single-arm conference abstract, and no guideline framework will exist for any of this until the phase 3 reads out.
Zolbetuximab is not a fallback: this tumor fails the 75% CDx cutoff and GLEAM was negative even above it, so off-label use has neither an eligibility nor an efficacy basis.

picks.intervention_label: olaparib maintenance, gated on the still-missing dedicated germline panel
picks.rationale: This pick is really about the test behind it. NCCN has recommended germline testing for every confirmed pancreatic cancer patient since 2019, and it has not been done here; 'no incidental findings' on tumor NGS is not a germline panel. A positive BRCA1/2 result opens the POLO maintenance route (PFS 7.4 vs 3.8 months, HR 0.53), the only biomarker-directed option in this disease with a randomized base and an FDA label. The panel is a blood draw orderable this week, and it gates a whole branch of the dossier.
primary_concerns: Even with a positive panel this patient sits outside the POLO population: POLO required at least 16 weeks of first-line platinum without progression, and this tumor progressed about 4 months after platinum-containing adjuvant therapy, so a platinum re-response would have to be demonstrated first.
Pre-test probability is low; roughly 5-7% of unselected PDAC carries a germline BRCA1/2 variant.
POLO's final OS was null (19.0 vs 19.2 months), so the honest framing even in a carrier is chemotherapy-free time, not survival gain.

notes: Guideline audit, checked live this round since the dossier can go stale faster than guidelines update. NCCN Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma v2.2026 (April 22, 2026) is the newest version I could verify from outside the paywall; one search hinted a later 2026 version may exist, worth an on-file check before the PI round. Positions I verified: (1) NCCN routes recurrence under 6 months from adjuvant completion to an alternative regimen, wants suspected recurrence confirmed by imaging and/or biopsy, and requires tissue confirmation before trial entry, so the EUS biopsy is guideline work, not extra caution. (2) Germline testing for all confirmed PDAC has been NCCN's position since 2019 and is still outstanding in this case. (3) NCCN's March 2026 update recommends tumor NGS profiling for all patients who are candidates for anti-cancer therapy, which covers re-profiling the recurrence. (4) CLDN18.2 appears only in NCCN Gastric/Esophageal v3.2026 at the 75% cutoff; no guideline anywhere addresses CLDN18.2 testing in PDAC. (5) No guideline yet names daraxonrasib or any KRAS-directed therapy in PDAC; the NDA was accepted July 2026, so that will change. (6) ESMO-MCBS is validated only for the first-line regimens here (FOLFIRINOX 5, NALIRIFOX 2, gem/nab-paclitaxel 3, all v1.1); nothing second-line carries a score and I quoted none. On NALIRIFOX: on paper it is a first-line option if this is called treatment-naive metastatic disease, but it re-runs three components of a regimen this tumor progressed through inside 4 months, and the recurrence pathway's switch-regimens logic argues against that reading, so I left it off. The Y220C reactivators and mKRAS vaccines are trial-only routes with no guideline standing, and PYNNACLE's registrational cohort excludes KRAS-SNV tumors, which closes rezatapopt monotherapy to this patient regardless.
